question: What is the main job of the mucus layer inside your gut?

options.A: To produce digestive enzymes that break down dietary fats
options.B: To absorb complex carbohydrates straight into your bloodstream
options.C: To speed up how fast waste moves through the colon
options.D: To trap bicarbonate and protect your stomach cells from harsh acid

explanation: Think of mucus as a protective shield! It holds bicarbonate right against your stomach lining to neutralize strong digestive acids so they don't harm your cells. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h1)

question: What happens when the tight seals (tight junctions) between cells in your gut get damaged?

options.A: Your body completely stops making digestive enzymes
options.B: Nutrient absorption shoots up because the spaces get wider
options.C: Peristalsis speeds up to push the damaged tissue out
options.D: Harmful substances leak into your body tissue and bloodstream

explanation: Tight junctions act like brick-and-mortar seals between your gut cells. When they break, unwanted substances slip through into the body, which can trigger inflammation. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h1)

question: How does the lower esophageal sphincter help protect you from GERD (heartburn)?

options.A: It acts like a muscular valve that stops stomach acid from flowing upward
options.B: It neutralizes food before it drops into the stomach
options.C: It secretes thick mucus to coat the top of the stomach
options.D: It controls how fast food leaves the stomach for the small intestine

explanation: The lower esophageal sphincter is your body's one-way valve. It stays tightly closed and only opens to let food travel down into the stomach. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h2)

question: Why can taking regular doses of NSAIDs (like ibuprofen) lead to stomach ulcers?

options.A: They block protective chemicals (prostaglandins) that help build stomach mucus
options.B: They paralyze the smooth muscles responsible for stomach movement
options.C: They directly increase the total amount of acid in your stomach
options.D: They force the lower esophageal sphincter to stay wide open all day

explanation: NSAIDs block helpful prostaglandins, which strips away your stomach's natural mucus and bicarbonate armor, leaving the tissue vulnerable to acid damage. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h2)

question: Which feature is unique to Crohn's disease when compared to ulcerative colitis?

options.A: It is caused directly by a specific bacterial infection
options.B: Damage is strictly limited to the inner lining of the colon
options.C: It features patchy 'skip lesions' and inflammation through all layers of the bowel wall
options.D: Inflammation is continuous and always starts from the rectum

explanation: Crohn's can affect the entire thickness of the bowel wall (transmural) and likes to leave healthy patches of tissue right next to diseased ones (skip lesions). [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h3)

question: Which part of the digestive tract does ulcerative colitis mainly affect?
explanation: Ulcerative colitis stays in the large intestine. It starts down in the rectum and can spread upward in a steady, continuous line. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is the main underlying issue in a patient with gastroparesis?

options.A: Severe inflammation and sores in the small bowel lining
options.B: Delayed stomach emptying even though there is no physical blockage
options.C: A total loss of the protective mucus barrier in the stomach
options.D: Food moving so fast it goes straight into the colon

explanation: In gastroparesis, the stomach is just too slow at emptying its contents. There's no tumor or physical blockage—it's usually a muscle or nerve issue! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why do patients with poorly controlled diabetes often develop delayed stomach emptying (gastroparesis)?

options.A: High sugar levels destroy specific gut cells through sudden local infections
options.B: Excess sugar physically coats the stomach lining and blocks food
options.C: High blood sugar damages the nerves (like the vagus nerve) that tell stomach muscles to move
options.D: Diabetes causes the stomach to make too much mucus, slowing digestion down

explanation: Over time, high blood sugar harms delicate nerves around the body. When the vagus nerve gets damaged, it can't send proper signals to make the stomach muscles contract. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is a classic warning sign in a patient experiencing acute mesenteric ischemia (lack of blood flow to the gut)?

options.A: Mild cramping that only shows up after eating fatty foods
options.B: A rigid, board-like belly with absolutely no pain
options.C: Painless bloody diarrhea with a high fever
options.D: Severe, agonizing belly pain that feels much worse than what you see on a physical exam

explanation: Because lack of oxygen seriously irritates the gut nerves, patients feel blinding pain, but when you press gently on their belly, it might still feel surprisingly soft at first. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h5)

question: What happens immediately to intestinal tissue when a mesenteric artery gets blocked?

options.A: The stomach instantly starts overproducing protective mucus
options.B: The tissue is starved of oxygen and begins to die (hypoxia and necrosis)
options.C: The tight junctions in the small intestine heal very rapidly
options.D: The lower esophageal sphincter permanently relaxes

explanation: Blood carries vital oxygen. Cut off that arterial supply, and the bowel tissue quickly starves, leading to tissue damage and death if not fixed. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h5)

question: What is the main difference between a mechanical bowel obstruction and a functional ileus?

options.A: A mechanical obstruction causes no pain, while an ileus causes severe cramps
options.B: A mechanical obstruction has a physical block, while an ileus happens when bowel movement simply stops without a block
options.C: An ileus is caused by scar tissue, while a mechanical obstruction is caused by high sugar
options.D: A mechanical obstruction affects only the colon; an ileus affects only the stomach

explanation: A mechanical block is something physical like a tumor or scar tissue getting in the way. An ileus is lazy bowel—the muscles just pause their normal movement without any physical wall. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h6)

question: Why do patients with celiac disease often have fatty, bulky stools (steatorrhea)?

options.A: The stomach makes too much acid, breaking down fats too fast
options.B: The liver stops making bile salts completely
options.C: The large intestine pulls way too much water out of the stool
options.D: Damaged tiny finger-like projections (villi) in the gut cannot absorb digested fats properly

explanation: Celiac disease flattens out the absorptive villi in your small intestine. Without those working structures, fats pass right through unabsorbed, making stools bulky and fatty. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h6)

question: What does 'coffee-ground emesis' (vomit that looks like coffee grounds) usually tell you during an assessment?

options.A: There is a complete blockage in the lower colon
options.B: The patient took too many oral iron supplements with food
options.C: The pancreas is inflamed and backing up into the stomach
options.D: There is upper GI bleeding, and the blood has been sitting in stomach acid

explanation: When bleeding happens in the upper GI tract, stomach acid reacts with the hemoglobin in the blood, turning it dark and giving vomit that classic coffee-ground texture. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h7)

question: Which nursing finding in a patient with belly pain is most urgent and needs an immediate call to the doctor?

options.A: A single episode of greenish-yellow vomit with food in it
options.B: A rigid, board-like belly with severe tenderness when you let go (rebound tenderness)
options.C: Mild nausea when the patient tries to sip water
options.D: Slowing bowel sounds heard four hours after surgery

explanation: A board-like rigid belly is a red flag for peritonitis (inflammation of the abdominal lining), which can rapidly progress to life-threatening sepsis if ignored. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h7)
